summary: Dedicated pool throughput suppression caused by silent-tenant heartbeat damping
description:
Issue summary: BrightScribe reported a sustained P99 throughput degradation for their dedicated pool during midday on 2026-03-12. Impact: degraded request throughput and elevated queuing leading to increased tail latency for inference requests. Root behaviour appears to be the autoscaler suppressing scale-ups due to misleading heartbeat-derived utilization signals from one or more silent tenants.

Impact details:
- Customer-facing: increased request backpressure, timeouts for a subset of long-lived streams, and ~25% drop in p50 throughput for routed model 'redwood/longform-16k'.
- Internal: autoscaler did not trigger expected burst additions for ~18 minutes despite GPU queue depth > 90% for several allocation groups.

Environment: Dedicated capacity, reserved pool id rp-47, us-east, auto-scale policy 'midday-burst' with predictive window enabled.

Observed by: BrightScribe Support and console alerting (route p99 queue depth alert).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Route sustained 1.5x baseline traffic of small- and long-form streams to a reserved pool with predictive autoscale enabled.
2) Start a silent/low-IO tenant process that maintains heartbeats but produces negligible packet I/O (simulated via sidecar shim that replies to health probes only).
3) Observe autoscaler decisions and GPU allocation logs over 15 minutes; check per-tenant heartbeat and allocation weighting logs.
4) Verify that predictive autoscaler avoids additional allocation despite queue depth rising above scale thresholds.
observed_metrics_and_logs:
- Autoscaler logs (autoscaler-controllers): repeated decisions 'scale: suppressed: low_active_weight' with reason 'heartbeat_pulse_low_io'.
- GPU allocator logs (gpu-manager): 'tenant_affinity=sticky' and 'available_slots=0' while 'queue_depth' climbs to 94%.
- Serving-runtime traces: continuous short-lived slot holds from tenant T-132 and a burst of many small streams causing slot fragmentation.
- Customer console screenshot referenced in linked Confluence runbook.
- No driver crashes or 5xx at infra layer; errors are queued timeouts from application layer.
investigation_notes: 03/12 11:10 - Support (Aisha): Customer reported sudden degradation at 11:05 local. Attached console timeline and request IDs.
03/12 11:18 - SRE (Ben): Correlated alert to reserved pool rp-47. Noted autoscaler logs showing repeated suppression flags tied to heartbeat-derived active-weight metric.

03/12 11:25 - Eng (Diego Morales): Dumped allocation state; found tenant T-132 registering heartbeats at expected cadence but emitting near-zero I/O. This created 'active' but effectively idle occupant for slot-weighting calculations.

03/12 11:31 - Eng (Priya Patel): Confirmed predictive autoscaler uses last N heartbeat pulses to compute expected demand; silent heartbeat clients skew expected_utilization downwards because they appear as 'active' but consume zero CPU/GPU until real traffic arrives.

03/12 11:40 - Hypothesis: Silent-heartbeat tenants are reducing the autoscaler's inferred demand variance, causing suppression of burst allocations until queued demand crosses a higher threshold. This leads to transient throughput starvation for other tenants.

03/12 11:52 - Temporary mitigation attempted: Increase autoscale aggressiveness for rp-47 via manual override (force-add 2 slots). Immediate improvement in p50 throughput observed; queuing dropped to normal ranges.
03/12 12:05 - Confirmed reproduction in staging cluster by running a heartbeat-shim service that responds to health checks only. Autoscaler suppressed expected allocation until manual override.

2026-03-12 11:28 - Ben Carter (SRE): Investigating reserved pool rp-47. Autoscaler logs show suppressed scale-ups with 'heartbeat_pulse_low_io' reason. Escalating to serving-runtime and autoscaler owners.

2026-03-12 11:33 - Diego Morales (Serving Eng): Found tenant T-132 active flag set but zero IO. Might be a tenant-side shim/SDK bug keeping TCP connections but not streaming. Requesting customer to check their SDK or sidecar behavior.

2026-03-12 11:45 - Customer (BrightScribe, Sarah Lee): We deployed a new sidecar last night; will rollback and test. Please advise if we should restart connections.\nCustomer note: This impacts high-priority flows for our transcription pipeline.

2026-03-12 12:15 - Priya Patel (Autoscaler): Adding follow-up fix to treat 'heartbeat with low outbound packets' as lower confidence for active-weight calculations. We'll propose a configurable threshold to avoid suppression by silent tenants.
2026-03-12 12:40 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer validated rollback of their sidecar; their traffic returns to normal. Asking for permanent fix and postmortem timeline.

2026-03-13 09:00 - Ben Carter (SRE): Creating rollout patch for autoscaler and scheduling canary in staging tomorrow. Preparing postmortem and recommended mitigation steps for customers with sidecars.
action_items: Hotfix: Autoscaler change to ignore heartbeat-only tenants when outbound-packet-rate < 1 pkt/s for the last 30s (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-14)
Customer guidance: Add snippet to SDK/sidecar to produce a minimal periodic probe packet when an active session is expected to generate traffic (owner: Support Docs, ETA: 2026-03-16)
Follow-up: Add metric 'heartbeat_io_confidence' to autoscaler telemetry and surface in Console (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-03-21)
Postmortem: Draft and share with BrightScribe and internal incident channel (#incidents) (owner: Ben, ETA: 2026-03-15)
Backport: Apply fix to autoscaler stable branch and coordinate Dedicated safe deploy window (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-18)
Test: Add chaos test in staging that simulates silent-heartbeat tenants and validates autoscaler doesn't suppress scale-ups incorrectly (owner: QA, ETA: 2026-03-20)
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround: manual slot increase for rp-47 restored throughput. Root cause: autoscaler's active-weight calculation treated persistent but low-IO heartbeats as evidence of capacity being 'in-use', which suppressed predictive scale-ups. Permanent remediation path: implement heartbeat IO-confidence metric and threshold, update autoscaler to down-weight heartbeat-only tenants, add SDK guidance for emitting minimal outbound packets when sessions are live. Scheduled hotfix and canary rollout. Customer confirmed rollback of faulty sidecar fixed immediate issue on their side.
final_status: Monitoring after deploy; waiting on autoscaler canary results. Postmortem scheduled.
